issues.description: matrix-copy initializes new-data with integer 0. For floating-point matrices, 0.0 is preferred for type consistency.

files_reviewed.notes: Solid implementation of LU, QR, and Cholesky. Correct handling of partial pivoting and singular matrices.

issues.description: sparse-coo-add-impl uses a dense accumulator vector of size (* rows cols). This causes O(N^2) memory usage, leading to exhaustion for large sparse matrices.
sparse-csr-mul uses a dense accumulator vector of size (* ma nb). This defeats the purpose of sparse matrix multiplication for large matrices.
dense->sparse-coo uses quotient and remainder in a loop; maintaining separate counters would be more efficient for large indices.

files_reviewed.notes: While the format definitions are correct, the arithmetic operations fail to respect the sparse nature of the data, making them unusable for large-scale problems.

issues.description: *current-tape* parameter is defined but unused in arithmetic operations (lines 118-240). Operations extract tape from inputs instead.
Arithmetic operations do not check if inputs 'a' and 'b' share the same tape, which can lead to corrupted gradients if values from different AD scopes are mixed.
traced-pow only supports constant exponents. Differentiating with respect to the exponent is not supported.

files_reviewed.notes: Well-documented reverse-mode AD. The use of parameters for scoping is good, but the tape management logic is slightly inconsistent.

issues.description: ifft-radix2-inplace! has an empty termination expression in the stage loop. While valid, it is less idiomatic than providing the vector as a return value.
zero-pad guesses the zero type by inspecting the first element of the input. This fails to distinguish complex/real if the input vector is empty.

files_reviewed.notes: Clean and correct implementation of DFT/FFT. Good separation between naive and radix-2 algorithms.

summary: Review complete. High severity memory allocation issues found in sparse.ss. reverse-diff.ss has architectural inconsistencies in tape management. matrix-decomp.ss and dft.ss are high quality with only minor style issues.
